mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: an unported branch of this command: applying a tool requires doapply()'s arm for object type 286

summary: Applying a blessed lump of royal jelly is refused after object selection because apply.c:doapply() lacks its named arm and use_royal_jelly() is not ported. C then prompts for an egg and, for the recorded killer bee egg, changes its species to queen bee and produces the source quiver message; the blessed-parent marker is set only when the egg’s spe field is zero. The helper consumes the jelly and spends a turn. The same source helper is also reached from #rub; its cursed branch depends on the still-unported timeout.c:kill_egg().

source.branch: After #apply or #rub selects a lump of royal jelly, use_royal_jelly() splits one unit from a stack if needed, removes it from inventory, and prompts for an egg. Cancellation restores the jelly and returns ECMD_CANCEL. For a selected egg, killer bee species changes to queen bee before the cursed check; cursed jelly kills the egg and consumes itself. Otherwise, a non-NON_PM egg without a hatch timer gets attach_egg_hatch_timeout(), blessed jelly sets spe=2 unless the egg was laid by the hero, the quiver message depends on timer, parent-marker, or species changes, and the jelly is consumed with ECMD_TIME.
callers: nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:doapply() case LUMP_OF_ROYAL_JELLY (4262-4264) calls use_royal_jelly(&obj); js/apply.js:doapply() is reached through js/cmd.js:runApplyCommand() (3302-3304) and the doapply command dispatch (5150-5151).

nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:dorub() food-class branch (1796-1804) calls use_royal_jelly(&obj); js/apply.js:dorub() is reached through js/cmd.js:runRubCommand() (3309-3310) and the dorub command dispatch (5152-5153).

nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:use_royal_jelly() supplies jelly_ok to invent.c:getobj() for the secondary egg prompt (3629-3631); js/invent.js:getobj() invokes the callback to rank selectable inventory objects.
dependencies: mkobj.c:splitobj() returns the single jelly object when splitting a stack; js/obj.js:splitobj() is implemented. Preserve the freeinv-before-secondary-prompt ordering, inventory restoration on cancellation (unsplitobj/update_inventory or addinv_nomerge), and source pointer clearing after consumption (setnotworn/obfree). The corresponding JS helpers are present in js/invent.js, js/obj.js, and js/worn.js.

timeout.c:attach_egg_hatch_timeout() is called only for a species egg without an active timer; js/timeout.js:attach_egg_hatch_timeout() is implemented and its bounded rnd() loop must remain in source order.

timeout.c:kill_egg() is a void call whose result is discarded in the cursed branch. No JS implementation exists; js/zap.js currently records note_unported('timeout.c kill_egg') for a separate caller. Per the gap rule, the cursed branch can record the same named gap and skip the call until that helper is ported.

evidence: challenges/evaluations/20261001125731-v16.json records the first stop at zero-based segment 0 step 64: 64/66 screens and cursors match and the PRNG logs match 4800/4804 calls. The mismatch is the existing UnsupportedApplyError boundary for object type 286 (LUMP_OF_ROYAL_JELLY) in apply.c:doapply().

The immutable C recording challenges/cases/v16/wizard-smears-blessed-royal-jelly-on-bee-egg.session.json shows step 64 key o opening “What do you want to rub the royal jelly on? [p or ?*]” and step 65 key p producing “You smear royal jelly all over your egg. The egg quivers briefly.” The recipe comment identifies the input sequence as applying wished blessed royal jelly to a killer bee egg.

nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:3615-3682 defines jelly_ok() and the whole use_royal_jelly() helper, including stack split, inventory rollback, killer-bee-to-queen-bee conversion, cursed and blessed branches, egg timer handling, jelly consumption, and ECMD_* result. The direct callers are apply.c:doapply() at 4262-4264 and apply.c:dorub() at 1796-1804.

js/apply.js:3867-3875 still lists LUMP_OF_ROYAL_JELLY in DOAPPLY_UNPORTED_NAMED_ARMS, and js/apply.js:4947-4950 throws for it after the doapply switch. js/apply.js:2218-2221 independently throws for royal jelly in dorub(). Add use_royal_jelly()/jelly_ok() in js/apply.js, wire both callers, and remove these two jelly-specific refusal paths while retaining the other named-arm gaps.

Production command routes are nethack-c/upstream/src/cmd.c:1677-1678 (apply key a) and 1835-1836 (rub extended command); js/cmd.js:3302-3310 and 5150-5153 route doapply and dorub to their apply.js handlers.

Source patch search `rg -n "use_royal_jelly|attach_egg_hatch_timeout|doapply|dorub|egg.*hatch" nethack-c/patches` returned no matches; this behavior comes directly from upstream apply.c and timeout.c.
jelly_ok() is pure: it returns GETOBJ_SUGGEST for EGG and GETOBJ_EXCLUDE for every other object or null. Pin both outcomes with source-derived tests when implementing this helper.
